## Phase 1 — orientation and a discriminating experiment (pre-claim; plan-review gate running)

**Step 0(a) duplicate sweep, all statuses.** No duplicate. Queries `Codex MCP PAT`,
`bearer_token_env_var`, `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX`, `omitting MCP server` return only this ticket and
the closed `unmythical-uninspired-olm`, which is the ticket that ESTABLISHED the canonical name.

**Step 0(b) reported-against floor.** `created_at` 1787856122601734001 ns → 2026-08-27T18:42:02Z
→ floor `a26a73277c8a`. **Step 0(c)** worktree at `a26a73277c8a` = `origin/main`, current.

**The repo contract is NOT drifted — this reframes AC2.** `git log <floor>..origin/main` over
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md` and `examples/mcp-clients/` is EMPTY, and the canonical name is already
consistent everywhere it appears: `docs/mcp-auth.md:286,294,322`, `docs/mcp-client-setup.md:26,74`,
`examples/mcp-clients/README.md:11,21`, `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:19`, and it is
already PINNED BY A TEST at `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:58`. The string
`REBAR_CODEX_PAT` appears NOWHERE in the repository.

So there is no repo-side inconsistency to single-source. The drift is entirely in the
machine-local `~/.codex/config.toml`, which is untracked and which no committed test can observe.
AC2 as written is already satisfied; the real gap is that nothing can DETECT a hand-edited client
config diverging from the contract, and that a GUI-launched macOS process does not inherit a
shell-exported variable at all — so even the CORRECT name would have been absent.

**Discriminating experiment — the live config had TWO deviations, not the one reported.** Its URL
is `https://.../mcp` (no trailing slash) against a documented `.../mcp/`. Before accepting the
missing-PAT hypothesis I tested whether the URL could independently explain the omission
(unauthenticated probes; no credential sent):

    /mcp   -> HTTP/2 401  www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token" ...
    /mcp/  -> HTTP/2 307  location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp

**The URL is ELIMINATED as a cause of this bug.** `/mcp` reaches the verifier and returns a clean
fail-closed 401 with a proper Bearer challenge, which is exactly the signature of a reachable
endpoint refusing an absent credential — consistent with the reported omission and with AC4's
expected behaviour. One cause, not two.

**But the probe surfaced a separate P1**, filed as `fernlike-toothsome-hen` and linked
`discovered_from`: the DOCUMENTED `/mcp/` form 307-redirects to the **http://** scheme with no
HSTS header. A 307 preserves method and body, so a client that retains its `Authorization` header
across a same-host scheme change would transmit the bearer PAT in plaintext. The uncomfortable
part: the drifted local config was on the SAFER URL than the one every doc and the committed
example specify.

Confirmed on this host: neither `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` nor `REBAR_CODEX_PAT` is set in the shell
environment. No credential value was read, printed, or transmitted at any point.

## Phase 1 EXIT — proven root cause (claimed; attestation certified)

**The root cause is not the misnamed variable. It is that the DOCUMENTED credential-delivery
mechanism structurally cannot reach a GUI-launched process, and nothing detects that.**

### Evidence

1. `docs/mcp-client-setup.md:26` and `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:9` both prescribe
   `export MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX="…"` — a **shell export**.
2. On this host the variable is absent from the **launchd** environment, which is what a
   GUI-launched macOS app inherits — under BOTH names:
       launchctl getenv MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX  -> unset
       launchctl getenv REBAR_CODEX_PAT       -> unset
3. It is absent from every shell rc file too (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.bash_profile`,
   `~/.profile`) — so it was never persistently exported at all, only ever transiently in one
   shell.
4. No document in the repo mentions `launchctl`, GUI launches, login shells, or environment
   inheritance. Grep across `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`, `docs/mcp-auth.md` and
   `examples/mcp-clients/` returns nothing.

### Why the 2026-08-25 smoke passed — the verification path is not the usage path

`creased-childlike-jackal` verified the three clients by invoking them from a **shell**
(`claude -p "call rebar list_tickets"`, `codex mcp list`). A shell-launched process DOES inherit
a transient export made in that same shell, so the smoke exercised the one path that works and
never touched the desktop path. The green smoke was therefore never evidence about GUI launches.

**This corrects the ticket's premise.** The description reasons that a passing 2026-08-25 smoke
makes the current state 'post-verification drift/regression rather than an unimplemented
endpoint'. On this evidence the GUI path was never verified and plausibly never worked; this is
closer to an unimplemented delivery path than to a regression. I am not asserting it never worked
— I cannot see the host's state on 08-25 — but the smoke does not support the regression claim.

### The name drift is real but NOT load-bearing

`~/.codex/config.toml` does say `bearer_token_env_var = "REBAR_CODEX_PAT"` against a canonical
`MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX`. Correcting it alone would change NOTHING: neither name is set anywhere
the GUI process can see. Any fix that only reconciles the name would leave the bug live while
appearing to address it.

### Consequence for AC2, which is already satisfied

The repo is already single-sourced on `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` (`docs/mcp-auth.md:286,294,322`,
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:26,74`, `examples/mcp-clients/README.md:11,21`,
`examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:19`) and it is ALREADY PINNED by
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:58`. `REBAR_CODEX_PAT` appears nowhere in
the repository. So AC2's 'single-source the canonical name' work does not exist; what is missing
is detection of a hand-edited LOCAL config that no committed test can observe.

### Legitimacy

This is a genuine defect, not working-as-designed: `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` presents Codex as a
supported client and gives a setup that cannot work for the desktop application, without
qualifying that it is CLI-only.

No credential value was read, printed, or transmitted at any point in this investigation.

comments.body:
## CORRECTION — my stated root cause was WRONG. Retracting the GUI-inheritance mechanism.

The operator reports that this failure came from `codex` run **directly from the user's
terminal**, not from the GUI desktop application.

That retracts the mechanism in my previous comment. I concluded the root cause was that a
GUI-launched macOS process does not inherit shell exports, and that the 2026-08-25 smoke passed
only because it used shell-launched clients — 'the verification path is not the usage path'. If
Codex was invoked from a terminal then it DOES inherit that shell's environment, both paths are
the same path, and my explanation cannot be the cause. I am withdrawing it rather than reshaping
it to fit.

I should have tested that premise instead of inheriting it. The ticket says 'Codex desktop
session' and 'the Codex desktop process environment', and I took 'desktop' at face value as
GUI-launched. The launchd evidence I gathered is real but explains nothing here.

### What the evidence still supports — and it is simpler

The finding that survives, and now carries the weight, is this one:

> `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` and `REBAR_CODEX_PAT` are absent from EVERY shell rc file checked
> (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`), and both are unset in an
> interactive shell on this host.

The documented setup (`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:26`,
`examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:9`) prescribes `export MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX="…"` — a
**transient** export. Nothing in the supported setup persists it. So the credential exists only
inside the single shell session where it was typed, and EVERY subsequent terminal — including the
one that produced this report — starts with no credential at all. Codex then has no bearer token
to send and omits the server.

That also re-explains the 08-25 smoke without my GUI story: the smoke exported the PAT in its own
shell and invoked the clients there, so it passed; the export died with that shell. The ticket's
'regression' framing is therefore closer to right than my correction claimed — though the more
accurate description is that the setup was never durable in the first place.

### Unchanged by this correction

- The repo IS already single-sourced on `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` and pinned by
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:58`; `REBAR_CODEX_PAT` appears NOWHERE in
  the repository. AC2's 'single-source the name' work still does not exist.
- The live config still names a variable the repo never defined, so even a persisted canonical
  export would not have been read.
- `fernlike-toothsome-hen` (the documented `/mcp/` URL 307-redirecting to plaintext `http://`)
  stands on its own unaffected evidence.

### Consequence for the fix

The fix direction narrows and gets more tractable: a durable, secret-safe credential path plus a
preflight that reports an unresolvable or non-canonically-named credential. I am dropping the
macOS/launchd-specific machinery I had begun designing around the wrong theory — it would have
encoded my error into the contract.

## Root cause CONFIRMED — and my environment probe was a direct measurement, not an analogy

The operator confirms Codex inherited the SAME environment this Claude Code session inherited.
That makes the check I already ran decisive rather than circumstantial:

    printenv MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX  -> unset
    printenv REBAR_CODEX_PAT       -> unset

I had treated that as suggestive evidence about a similar shell. It is not similar — it is the
same environment Codex ran in. The credential is simply absent, under either name.

### The proven account, in two parts

**Cause 1 (load-bearing): the credential is not present in the environment, and nothing in the
supported setup ever persists it.** `docs/mcp-client-setup.md:26` and
`examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:9` prescribe `export MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX="…"`, a
transient shell export. It appears in no rc file on this host (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`,
`~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`), so it survives only inside the shell where it was typed. Every
later shell — including the one that ran Codex — starts with nothing. Codex has no bearer token
to send, so it omits the server with `omitting MCP server without an exact ready client`.

**Cause 2 (compounding, not sufficient alone): the local config names a variable the repo never
defines.** `~/.codex/config.toml` says `bearer_token_env_var = "REBAR_CODEX_PAT"`;
`REBAR_CODEX_PAT` appears NOWHERE in this repository. So even a correctly persisted
`MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` would not be read by this config. Fixing either one alone leaves the
server omitted — which is exactly why a fix must address both, and why a diagnostic that checks
only one would report a false all-clear.

This is the smallest set of causes that explains every observed symptom: the omission itself, the
absence of `mcp__rebar__*` tools, and the 08-25 smoke having passed (it exported the PAT in its
own shell and invoked the clients there; the export died with that shell).

### Legitimacy

A genuine defect against an authoritative source, not a misunderstanding:
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md` presents a setup procedure whose credential step does not survive the
shell it is run in, while presenting Codex as a supported client. The bug ticket's own expected
behaviour — 'securely makes that credential available to the ... Codex process' — is the contract
being violated.

comments.body:
Implemented locally on branch 71e7-codex-mcp-pat (commit fe4b0b6c1f16, not pushed).

New `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_mcp_client.py` (353 LOC) — a stdlib-only, OS-agnostic scan of the Codex / Copilot / Claude Code MCP client configs. Public contract: `scan_mcp_clients(*, home=None, env=None) -> list[dict]` and `render_text(findings) -> list[str]`, plus `has_blocking_mcp_client(findings)`. Findings carry `client` / `kind` / `detail` / `severity` (+ `path`, `env_var`). The two headline kinds are `pat-unresolvable` (config names a bearer env var that is unset/empty in `env`; detail names the variable and states the durable-delivery remedy) and `stale-pat-env-name` (config's bearer var is not the canonical one for that client; detail names the canonical target). They are reported INDEPENDENTLY, so staleness fires even when the stale variable resolves. Supporting kinds: `config-missing`, `config-unreadable`, `server-absent`, `pat-not-referenced`, `pat-literal-in-config`, `ok`.

No credential VALUE can reach a finding or rendered line: configs are read for env-var NAMES only, and a name is resolved against the environment purely as a truthiness test — the value is never bound, formatted, or returned. A header that does not reference a variable is reported by kind without echoing the header.

Wired into `doctor.py` alongside `doctor_locks` / `doctor_mapping` (text section + `mcp_client_findings` in the JSON envelope). Deliberately ADVISORY for the exit code: these findings are read from the operator's HOME rather than the store, so folding them into doctor's exit would make a store-health gate depend on whichever client configs sit on the box (it also broke six existing hermetic doctor tests). `has_blocking_mcp_client` is the seam for a caller that does want to gate.

Docs: `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` gains "Make the export DURABLE — a bare `export` is not setup" (rc file vs secret manager, chmod/never-commit warnings) and a section describing the two doctor findings. The three committed example configs now point at it instead of implying a one-off export is sufficient.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_doctor_mcp_client.py`, 20 observable-behaviour tests (stale rejected, unresolvable reported, empty-is-unresolvable, stale-fires-when-resolvable, both-independent, healthy clean, missing/malformed degrade, no-rebar-entry, both `$VAR` and `${VAR}` forms, literal flagged without echo, no-value-leak, render shape, severity classification, env default).

Verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_doctor_mcp_client.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py -q` = 30 passed; `make lint` exit 0 (complexity ratchet: active=40 new=0 increased=0); `make typecheck` = Success, 678 files. Running `rebar doctor` on this box reproduces the reported production fault exactly: codex `stale-pat-env-name` + `pat-unresolvable` naming REBAR_CODEX_PAT and the canonical MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX, with no value printed.

Not pushed to Gerrit and not submitted, per instruction.

## Context / observed failure
On 2026-08-27 at approximately 11:37 PDT, a new Codex desktop session in `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` started without the configured remote Rebar MCP server. The runtime tool catalog contained no `mcp__rebar__*` tools and logged:

```text
omitting MCP server without an exact ready client server_name=rebar
```

The active `~/.codex/config.toml` entry points at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` but declares `bearer_token_env_var = "REBAR_CODEX_PAT"`. The committed client contract in `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`, `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml`, and the completed client-wiring ticket `unmythical-uninspired-olm` instead uses `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX`. Neither name is present in the Codex desktop process environment. A live Codex MCP smoke had passed on 2026-08-25 under `creased-childlike-jackal`, so the current state is post-verification drift/regression rather than an unimplemented endpoint.

## Impact
Codex agents silently lose all Rebar tracker tools at session startup and must fall back to the local CLI. That breaks the canonical MCP routing path for tracker reads/writes and makes the configured server appear present while it is unusable. The current diagnostic does not identify the credential name or remediation.

## Reproduction
1. Configure `[mcp_servers.rebar]` for the production `/mcp` endpoint with `bearer_token_env_var` naming a variable absent from the desktop application environment.
2. Launch a new Codex desktop session.
3. Start a thread in the rebar checkout and inspect the MCP tool catalog.
4. Observe that Rebar is omitted with no `mcp__rebar__*` tools, while other MCP servers initialize.

## Expected behavior
The supported Codex setup uses one canonical PAT environment name and securely makes that credential available to the GUI-launched Codex process. Rebar initializes at startup and exposes its tools. If the credential is unavailable, startup reports an actionable error naming the missing variable and the supported setup/rotation path; no secret is logged.

## Plan
- Trace how the live-smoke Codex credential was injected and how the active config later drifted to `REBAR_CODEX_PAT`.
- Single-source the canonical Codex PAT environment name across examples, docs, templates, and any operator setup/materialization path.
- Provide a durable, secret-safe launch or preflight path for GUI-launched Codex sessions and an actionable missing-credential diagnostic.
- Add regression coverage for config-name consistency and the desktop startup/preflight path, then repeat the authenticated live read-tool smoke.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a fresh supported Codex desktop setup and a valid provisioned Codex PAT, when Codex launches, then the Rebar MCP server reaches ready state and a real read tool returns a structured result.
- [ ] The canonical Codex PAT environment name is identical across the active setup path, committed examples, documentation, templates, and tests; stale alternate names are rejected or migrated with a clear message.
- [ ] Given the PAT is missing from the GUI application environment, startup or a mandatory preflight fails clearly and names the missing variable plus the supported remediation, without printing the PAT.
- [ ] Given an invalid PAT, the production endpoint remains fail-closed with HTTP 401 and the client surfaces an authentication error.
- [ ] Automated regression coverage fails if the Codex config name and credential-delivery path drift apart again.

## Security / compatibility
Do not inline, commit, or log the bearer PAT. Preserve the production static-bearer verifier and its fail-closed behavior; this bug concerns client configuration and credential delivery, not weakening authentication.

- [ ] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** a Codex session started from a terminal lists `mcp__rebar__*` tools and one read tool returns a real structured result.
      Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed server at
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` and recorded in a ticket comment naming
      the tool(s) called, the arguments, and the actual response. A passing local test is
      NOT sufficient, and neither is a merged change: the container must have redeployed
      and served the call. This exists because a fix here was previously reported complete
      on the strength of a merge while the deployed behaviour was still broken.
compiled_state.title: Codex omits Rebar MCP at startup when the desktop PAT environment is missing or misnamed
